pr_title: drivers: usb: udc: add NuMaker series USBD controller driver
pr_body:
This is to add UDC driver for Nuvoton NuMaker series USBD controller.

Verified samples include:
- zephyr/samples/subsys/usb/cdc_acm
- zephyr/samples/subsys/usb/console
- zephyr/samples/subsys/usb/hid-mouse
- zephyr/samples/subsys/usb/mass

Fixes: #74660
pr_comments:
1. Rebase on main to get device id support #75747 
2. Change usbd clock source to hirc48m so that core clock and PLL are not limited to multiple of 48MHz which usbd requires
3. Fix with end of control data out stage. With #74021 getting in, `net_buf` can over-allocate for `UDC_BUF_GRANULARITY` requirement and now `net_buf_tailroom()` cannot reflect free buffer room exactly as allocate request.

@ccli8 I see only `boards/nuvoton/numaker_pfm_m467` has USB controller, please add `usbd` test feature for this board.

```diff
diff --git a/boards/nuvoton/numaker_pfm_m467/numaker_pfm_m467.yaml b/boards/nuvoton/numaker_pfm_m467/numaker_pfm_m467.yaml
index d668f51facb..a7e26960ae6 100644
--- a/boards/nuvoton/numaker_pfm_m467/numaker_pfm_m467.yaml
+++ b/boards/nuvoton/numaker_pfm_m467/numaker_pfm_m467.yaml
@@ -13,4 +13,5 @@ ram: 512
 flash: 1024
 supported:
   - gpio
+  - usbd
 vendor: nuvoton
```

> I see only boards/nuvoton/numaker_pfm_m467 has USB controller, please add usbd test feature for this board.

Added usbd into the numaker_pfm_m467 board.

issue_context.title: drivers: usb: Port `usb_dc_numaker` to `UDC API`
issue_context.body:
In order for the `USB_DEVICE_STACK_NEXT` to become the default, existing USB device drivers must be ported to it.
See #42066 for additional details.

Note that if this driver is not ported by Zephyr 4.0.0, this hardware will not work with the default USB stack in 4.0.0.

Example ports:
- udc_kinetis and udc_nrf PR #38679
- udc_it82xx2 PR #65792
- udc_dwc2 PR  #64943
- udc_stm32 PR #53408
- udc_mcux PR #70401

Skeleton file to use as a starting point:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/drivers/usb/udc/udc_skeleton.c

Documentation:
https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/connectivity/usb/device_next/usb_device.html
https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/connectivity/usb/device_next/api/index.html
comments: Thanks. The port to `USB_DEVICE_STACK_NEXT` is scheduled.

review_comments:
This sounds wrong. Is the `SE0` simply some crazy naming to "disable D+ pull-up"? The device cannot initiate bus reset on its own - it is always host responsibility. The Full-Speed device can disable the D+ pull-up which will cause the pull-downs at the host to discharge the lines (and create SE0).

Is the NuMaker USBD datasheet publicly available? Does the HW allow disabling D+ pull-up?

It is [publicly available](https://www.nuvoton.com/products/microcontrollers/arm-cortex-m4-mcus/m467-ethernet-crypto-series/?group=Document&tab=2) (check the title **M463/M467 Series Technical Reference Manual** and the IP is **USB 1.1 Device Controller (USBD)**).

According to the h/w spec, the effect is to force D+/D- to low, so it can simulate disconnecting device from host. Excerpt the description:

> A software-disconnect function is also supported for this USB controller. It is used to simulate the disconnection of this device from the host. If user enables SE0 bit (USBD_SE0), the USB controller will force the output of USB_D+ and USB_D- to level low and its function is disabled. After disabling the SE0 bit, host will enumerate the USB device again.

I wonder if setting `USBD_SE0` is really standard compliant. The specification describes the disconnection as D+ pull-up removal. Anyway, device doesn't have option to disable the pull-up so this is what the software has to do.
